medicina.titulo: PET/CT imaging provides new insights into type 1 diabetes progression
medicina.resumo: A novel molecular imaging approach that measures beta-cell mass in the pancreas can offer valuable insights into the progression of type 1 diabetes, according to new research published in the Journal of Nuclear Medicine. The study found that individuals who have had type 1 diabetes for less than seven years have higher total beta-cell mass and function, larger pancreatic volume and lower intrapancreatic fat compared to those who have had the disease for longer. This valuable information, paired with functional tests, has the potential to significantly improve clinical trials of new therapeutic interventions.

medicina.titulo: Fiocruz promove seminário internacional sobre cannabis medicinal no Museu do Amanhã
medicina.resumo: Fiocruz promove seminário internacional sobre cannabis medicinal no Museu do Amanhã A Fiocruz e a Associação de Apoio à Pesquisa e Pacientes de Cannabis Medicinal (Apepi) promovem, no início de dezembro (5 e 6/12), a 4ª edição do Seminário Internacional Cannabis Medicinal: Um Olhar para o Futuro . O evento será realizado no Museu do Amanhã, no Rio de Janeiro, e tem como objetivo ampliar o diálogo entre ciência, sociedade civil e poder público, considerando o papel das associações de pacientes na garantia do direito à saúde e na construção de alternativas de acesso ao tratamento. Realizado pelo Programa Institucional de Políticas sobre Drogas, Direitos Humanos e Saúde Mental (PDHSM) da Presidência da Fiocruz, o evento traz quatro temas como eixos principais: a incorporação de tratamentos ao Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS); a ampliação do acesso; os avanços da pesquisa científica; e a regulamentação das associações de pacientes. Além disso, pretende aprofundar o debate sobre os desafios enfrentados pelas associações que atuam no acolhimento de pacientes e na produção de cannabis para fins terapêuticos, em especial, diante das demandas por regulamentação e segurança jurídica para essas i

medicina.titulo: Molecular backdoor destroys 'undruggable' protein driving rare childhood cancer
medicina.resumo: A secret molecular backdoor let researchers from Penn State College of Medicine destroy a protein that drives a rare and often fatal bone and soft tissue cancer in children and adolescents that often returns in treatment-resistant forms. Now, just three years after the discovery, a Phase I clinical trial is underway and, once complete, a Phase II trial to test the approach's efficacy in patients will follow shortly thereafter.

medicina.titulo: Potential limits of breast cancer screening policies across Southeast Asia identified
medicina.resumo: In Southeast Asia, breast cancer screening could have limited potential to reduce breast cancer mortality due to screening age eligibility not aligning with the actual ages at which women develop the disease, according to a study by the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore (NUS Medicine).

biologia.titulo: Evolution's balancing act—keeping genes in sync after genome duplication
biologia.resumo: Getting the right balance is important in all walks of life, whether it's a healthy combination of food groups in a balanced diet or a balanced mix of skills that allows a work or sports team to succeed.

biologia.titulo: DNA storage system holds data in living human cells and protects access with genetic decoys
biologia.resumo: University of Texas at Dallas researchers have developed a method for securely storing data in the DNA of living human cells while protecting the information from unauthorized access. The researchers describe the technology in a paper published online Oct. 21 in Nature Communications.

biologia.titulo: Cells can adjust gene activity to partly offset extra or missing chromosomes
biologia.resumo: When a cell loses or gains an extra chromosome, the activity of hundreds or even thousands of genes is affected. A new study published in Nature Communications shows that cells have a much greater ability than previously thought to compensate for such changes. The findings provide new insight into how genes are regulated and may help improve our understanding of how cancer cells cope with major changes in their genetic material.

biologia.titulo: Genetic analysis reveals peak orchid root fungal diversity at one of the most biodiverse places on Earth
biologia.resumo: The fungal communities living in the roots of epiphytic orchids vary with altitude, location and orchid species, according to research published in the journal Microbial Ecology. The study, conducted in Podocarpus National Park in southern Ecuador, found that mid-elevation forests harbor the greatest diversity of these microorganisms, while their richness decreases at higher elevations and their community composition differs.

robotica.titulo: How DARPA Challenged Teams to Bring Robots Into Disaster Triage
robotica.resumo: On 5 November, 10 teams descended upon a 52-acre mock town in College Station, Texas called Disaster City . They were there for a nine-day competition to see how well teams of robots and humans could navigate simulated catastrophes, like a market ravaged by a tornado and a nighttime strike on a military base. At stake? US $2.5 million in prize money. The scenarios were the final of the DARPA Triage Challenge , which the U.S. agency has been running for three years with the goal of saving more lives in urgent mass casualty events. Engineers from academia and industry have competed in elaborately staged mass casualty events , such as simulated combat zones and plane crash scenes. Teams spent years designing systems where autonomous ground robots and drones could help first responders find mock victims and decide the best way to care for them. “Triage is all about resources,” says Jeremy Pamplin , who managed the challenge for DARPA. Pamplin is a critical care physician and retired colonel who spent 28 years in the U.S. Army. In mass casualty events, medics race to assess trauma with finite resources and limited time. robotica.titulo: Swarm intelligence for surfaces: Miniature robots bring artificial skin to life
robotica.resumo: From responsive textiles that create a new tactile experience in gaming to interactive displays, soft robotic arms and intelligent factory conveyor systems—miniature robots made from thin polymer films could provide surfaces with a whole range of new and useful functions. Professor Gianluca Rizzello's research group at Saarland University is studying how such film-based robots work together beneath a silicone skin, acting collectively like artificial muscles and sensory nerves. Lightweight, flexible and powered solely by electricity, the system requires no bulky hydraulic or pneumatic equipment, external sensors, cameras or tangles of cables.

astrofisica.titulo: NASA's Hubble views ocean of stars in groundwork for Roman
astrofisica.resumo: An expanse of stars gleams in a rainbow of colors in these NASA Hubble Space Telescope images of the Milky Way. The images focus on an area of sky toward the galactic bulge, a densely packed, spherical region of stars that surrounds the center of a galaxy's disk. These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy.

The best Windows backup software includes file backup, sure, but also disk imaging and full image restore, as well as disaster recovery. Our picks for best Windows backup software are selected with all the must-haves of data backup and recovery in mind, so in the tragic event that your primary local data repository is compromised, you’re fully covered. Some of these work well (Restore Points, File History), others don’t (System Repair Disc, Recovery Drive). None are suitable for quick and easy disaster recovery — even the online backup that is available when you use Windows with a Microsoft cloud account. computadores_pessoais.titulo: Your Windows 11 PC is getting a speed boost thanks to major RAM cuts
computadores_pessoais.resumo: At the Ignite developer conference, Microsoft shared more details about its efforts to reduce memory usage in Windows 11, reports Windows Latest . According to the company, the Defender security program, the OneDrive cloud storage service, and the Purview data protection service now collectively use over 500 MB less RAM than before. Memory usage in Microsoft 365 has also been reduced by 360 MB. To achieve this, Microsoft reviewed which components need to be loaded into RAM and how different components can share resources. Rising memory prices are one of the reasons why Microsoft is focusing on improving performance on computers with 8 or 16 GB of RAM. However, users with better-equipped computers should also be able to benefit from these optimizations. Some of these improvements already rolled out as part of the October update for Windows 11.

inteligencia_artificial.titulo: One UI 9.5 vai ganhar recurso de IA que melhora fotos com zoom no celular
inteligencia_artificial.resumo: One UI 9.5 vai ganhar recurso de IA que melhora fotos com zoom no celular A Samsung está desenvolvendo uma ferramenta de inteligência artificial (IA) capaz de melhorar a qualidade de fotografias tiradas com zoom nos celulares Galaxy. O “ Zoom Enhancer” permitirá aprimorar a nitidez de imagens diretamente na Galeria do celular, mesmo após a captura. A novidade foi identificada pelo SamMobile nesta quarta-feira (25) na primeira versão beta da One UI 9.5 para a linha Galaxy S26. A ferramenta ainda está oculta no sistema e não pode ser acessada pelos participantes do programa de testes. Como funciona o Zoom Enhancer da Samsung? Diferentemente do zoom óptico, que utiliza as lentes da câmera para aproximar uma cena, o zoom digital recorta e amplia uma parte da imagem capturada pelo sensor. Esse processo pode resultar na perda de detalhes e na redução da nitidez da fotografia. O Zoom Enhancer utilizará o Galaxy AI para aprimorar tanto fotos tiradas com altos níveis de zoom quanto imagens de baixa resolução. energia_materiais.titulo: Nano-links stitch perovskite solar cell layers together, boosting stability while preserving efficiency
energia_materiais.resumo: A research team at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) has developed a novel interface engineering technology that addresses performance degradation in perovskite solar cells caused by interfacial mechanical failure. By forming nano-link networks across and within the interfacial layers of the solar cell, the technology significantly improves the mechanical reliability and stability of the devices while maintaining high power conversion efficiency.

energia_materiais.titulo: Bug ou desgaste real? One UI 9.5 vai resolver falha na bateria de celulares Galaxy
energia_materiais.resumo: Bug ou desgaste real? One UI 9.5 vai resolver falha na bateria de celulares Galaxy A Samsung deve corrigir um problema relacionado à saúde da bateria de celulares Galaxy com o lançamento da One UI 9.5. Desde a chegada da One UI 9.0, usuários relatam quedas anormais no percentual de saúde da bateria , inclusive em smartphones com poucas semanas de uso. A informação sobre a correção foi compartilhada nesta quarta-feira (25) pela equipe de suporte da Samsung na Turquia após um usuário enviar um relatório de erro pelo aplicativo Samsung Members. Em uma publicação no fórum da fabricante, o usuário relata casos de celulares que passaram a indicar 94% de saúde da bateria após apenas um mês de uso . A resposta da Samsung chegou cerca de duas semanas depois do envio do relatório. Bug ou desgaste prematuro da bateria? A Samsung não esclareceu se o problema está relacionado a um erro no cálculo da saúde da bateria ou se a One UI 9.0 está contribuindo para a degradação acelerada do componente. A saúde da bateria indica quanto da capacidade original de armazenamento de energia o componente ainda preserva. Isso representa cerca de 28% de todos os imóveis catalogados na experiência da Rockstar . Neste momento, você deve estar se perguntando quem contou todos os edifícios e espaços do título a menos de uma semana de seu lançamento e foi o usuário “Aileos”, no Reddit. Ele revela que das 5.588 obras presentes, ele conseguiu acessar 1.563 . O número supera o que já tinha sido apresentado nos vazamentos que o título sofreu ao longo dos anos. Em 2025, rumores indicavam 700 ambientes interativos — o que era visto como “utópico” e o equivalente a “ter expectativas altas” e “irreais”. A realidade trouxe mais do que o dobro . Se comparado a Grand Theft Auto V (2013), essa quantidade é ainda mais impressionante. Considerado por muitos como o game de mundo aberto “moderno” definitivo por uma década, o jogo tinha cerca de 100 áreas internas exploráveis.
